**Written Statement Regarding October 27 Afternoon Bus Run**

**To:** Mrs. Okafor  
**Copy to:** Darlene, Transportation Supervisor  
**From:** [Driver’s name], Bus 41, Route 9 Elementary  
**Date:** [Date submitted]  
**Subject:** Afternoon bus run involving Amara Okafor on Tuesday, October 27

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

I am writing in response to your complaint dated October 29, which Darlene gave me on November 3. I understand that this statement will be placed in my file and that you will receive a copy. I want to explain what happened from my point of view, including the steps I took to keep Amara safe and follow the district’s procedure.

First, I understand why this was frightening and upsetting for you. I have grandchildren, and I know I would be worried if a child I was expecting did not get off the bus. I am sorry that you and your family had such a difficult afternoon. I hope this statement helps explain why I returned Amara to Fairmont Elementary.

Amara is a kindergarten student at Fairmont Elementary and rides Bus 41 on Route 9 Elementary. She has a green tag on her bag, which indicates that an adult must be present at the stop before she can be released. My understanding of the district’s rule for kindergarten riders is that, if no adult is present at the stop, the student stays on the bus and returns to school, where the office contacts the parent.

On Tuesday, October 27, I arrived at the stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street at approximately 3:52 p.m. The scheduled arrival time was 3:50 p.m. I waited until approximately 3:55 p.m., but I did not see an adult at the corner. Because I could not see an adult there to receive Amara, I kept her on the bus in accordance with the procedure.

At approximately 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch. Gloria at dispatch called the school. At that point, I still had three stops to complete and 14 children on the bus. I could not leave the bus and those children unattended to look across the road.

I understand from your complaint that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and waved to me. I did not see you or your wave. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street. I understand that you were trying to get my attention, but from where I was, I did not see you.

After completing the remaining stops, I returned Amara to Fairmont Elementary at approximately 4:31 p.m. I personally walked her into the office and left her with Mrs. Petrakis.

While Amara was on the bus, she appeared fine. She was coloring on her folder and asked if she could ride some more. I told her that we were going on a little extra trip. I stayed focused on completing the route and getting her safely back to school.

I also want to address the concern that I drove away laughing. I was not laughing. As we pulled away, I was telling a fourth-grade student in seat 2 to sit back down. I understand how my actions may have looked from where you were, but I was not laughing about the situation.

I have been a school bus driver for 28 years and have never had a write-up. I take the safety of every child on my bus seriously. My decision that afternoon was not meant to cause you distress or keep Amara from you. I followed the procedure as I understand it because I could not see an adult at the stop.

I respectfully ask the transportation office to **preserve and review the available bus camera footage from the October 27 afternoon run**, including the footage at the Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street stop and as the bus pulled away. I believe it will help provide a clearer account of what happened.

Mrs. Okafor, I would like us to avoid another upsetting situation. When meeting Amara, please stand on the bus side of the street or step out of your car where I can clearly see you. That will help me know that she has an adult there to receive her.

I am glad to continue driving Amara, and I want to put this matter behind us and have a good relationship going forward. Thank you for taking the time to read my account.

Sincerely,

[Driver’s name]  
School Bus Driver, Bus 41  
Route 9 Elementary
